_note: AUTHORED practice questions for Part II's leveled Group Work, appended by scripts/generate-part-two.mjs. Keyed by CORE lesson id, then by target level (level1/level2/level3). Everything else in groupLevels is copied verbatim from the core lesson and its small-group variants; these are the only questions Part II owns, and they exist because no core practice pool contains a tape-diagram MODEL question (read the model, choose the expression) — every figure-bearing practice item is tagged sgFigure and drawn by small-group-visual-practice.js's 43-kind dispatcher, which has no tape-diagram case. Author them the same way a lesson config authors a multiple-choice item: choices, correctIndex, choiceFeedback for EVERY choice, explanation, a three-rung hint ladder, and the Spanish lane.

level1.stem: The model shows a 2-foot strip cut into 1/3-foot pieces. Which expression does the model represent, and how many pieces are there?
choiceFeedback: That multiplies. 2 × 1/3 finds 1/3 OF the strip, but the model cuts the strip up and counts the pieces.
You divided in the wrong order. The 2-foot strip is the amount being cut, so it goes first: 2 ÷ 1/3.
You divided by 3 instead of by 1/3. Dividing by 3 makes 3 long pieces; the model shows small 1/3-foot pieces, and there are more of them than 2.
level1.explanation: Each of the 2 feet holds three 1/3-foot pieces, so the model shows 6 pieces in all. Written as an expression that is 2 ÷ 1/3. Put a 1 under the 2, then Keep, Change, Flip: 2/1 × 3/1 = 6.
hints: Read the model first: how long is the whole strip, and how long is each small piece?
The model cuts a whole into equal small pieces and counts them. That is a division question — total ÷ piece size — so the total goes in front of the ÷ sign.
Count the 1/3-foot parts in both feet, then check it: put a 1 under the 2 and flip the 1/3 to get 2/1 × 3/1.
level1.stemEs: El modelo muestra una tira de 2 pies cortada en piezas de 1/3 de pie. ¿Qué expresión representa el modelo y cuántas piezas hay?
level1.explanationEs: Cada uno de los 2 pies contiene tres piezas de 1/3 de pie, así que el modelo muestra 6 piezas en total. Escrito como expresión es 2 ÷ 1/3. Pon un 1 debajo del 2 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 2/1 × 3/1 = 6.
hintsEs: Primero lee el modelo: ¿cuánto mide la tira entera y cuánto mide cada pieza pequeña?
El modelo corta un entero en piezas iguales y las cuenta. Esa es una pregunta de división — total ÷ tamaño de la pieza — así que el total va delante del signo ÷.
Cuenta las partes de 1/3 de pie en los dos pies y luego compruébalo: pon un 1 debajo del 2 y voltea el 1/3 para obtener 2/1 × 3/1.

level2.stem: The model shows a 4-foot rope cut into 1/5-foot pieces. Which expression does the model represent, and how many pieces are there?
choiceFeedback: That multiplies. 4 × 1/5 finds 1/5 OF the rope, but the model cuts the rope up and counts the pieces.
You divided in the wrong order. The 4-foot rope is the amount being cut, so it goes first: 4 ÷ 1/5.
You divided by 5 instead of by 1/5. Dividing by 5 makes 5 long pieces; the model shows small 1/5-foot pieces, and there are more of them than 4.
level2.explanation: Each of the 4 feet holds five 1/5-foot pieces, so the model shows 20 pieces in all. Written as an expression that is 4 ÷ 1/5. Put a 1 under the 4, then Keep, Change, Flip: 4/1 × 5/1 = 20.
hints: Read the model first: how long is the whole rope, and how long is each small piece?
The model cuts a whole into equal small pieces and counts them. That is a division question — total ÷ piece size — so the total goes in front of the ÷ sign.
Count the 1/5-foot parts in all four feet, then check it: put a 1 under the 4 and flip the 1/5 to get 4/1 × 5/1.
level2.stemEs: El modelo muestra una cuerda de 4 pies cortada en piezas de 1/5 de pie. ¿Qué expresión representa el modelo y cuántas piezas hay?
level2.explanationEs: Cada uno de los 4 pies contiene cinco piezas de 1/5 de pie, así que el modelo muestra 20 piezas en total. Escrito como expresión es 4 ÷ 1/5. Pon un 1 debajo del 4 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 4/1 × 5/1 = 20.
hintsEs: Primero lee el modelo: ¿cuánto mide la cuerda entera y cuánto mide cada pieza pequeña?
El modelo corta un entero en piezas iguales y las cuenta. Esa es una pregunta de división — total ÷ tamaño de la pieza — así que el total va delante del signo ÷.
Cuenta las partes de 1/5 de pie en los cuatro pies y luego compruébalo: pon un 1 debajo del 4 y voltea el 1/5 para obtener 4/1 × 5/1.
